ticket.title: Gates and doc checks should take a --baseline rev so pre-existing drift is not confused with mine
ticket.description: Observed 2026-11-06: after touching a crate I could not tell whether a fmt failure or a docs drift was mine or already on main. I answered it with a git stash round-trip and a manual re-run, twice (dado fmt drift, common docs drift), and once by checking out HEAD~1 files in place. Both are slow and easy to get wrong. 'chalkline docs check --baseline <rev>' and 'outfeed gate --baseline <rev>' would report which findings are new since that revision, which is the only question an agent or a reviewer actually has. It would also make a red gate on main actionable ('this one is pre-existing, file it') instead of a guess.
